title: Moules Frites
subtitle: Mussels steamed in white wine with chips
excerpt: The Belgian national dish that has conquered the world: fresh mussels steamed open in white wine, shallots, garlic, and parsley until they open and the cooking liquid becomes a fragrant, briny broth. Served with thick-cut chips for dipping.

recipe.sourceNotes: Moules frites (mussels and chips) is claimed by both Belgium and France, with Belgians particularly possessive about the frites component: Belgian chips are different, made from specific floury potato varieties and fried twice for a crisp exterior and fluffy interior. The combination of mussels with chips is particularly associated with Belgium, where it is eaten at dedicated moules-frites restaurants and also as a street food at friteries (chip stands). The classic preparation is moules marinière (sailor's mussels): steamed in white wine, shallots, and parsley. Variations include moules à la crème (with cream added to the broth), moules au roquefort, and moules with blue cheese. The key to good mussels is freshness: they should be live, smell of the sea, and close when tapped.

content.text: Discard any mussels that remain open when tapped sharply; they are dead and should not be eaten. Steam over high heat in a very large pan with a tight lid so the steam is trapped and the mussels cook quickly and evenly. Do not overcook: once the shells are fully open, they are done. Overcooked mussels are rubbery and shrink to nothing.

items.preparation: scrubbed, debearded; discard any open ones that don't close when tapped

content.text: Melt the butter in a very large pot over medium heat. Cook the shallots and garlic for 3 minutes until soft. Pour in the wine, increase to high heat, and let it bubble for 1 minute.

Add all the mussels and put on the lid immediately. Cook over high heat for 3 to 4 minutes, shaking the pan once halfway through, until all the mussels have opened. Discard any that remain firmly closed.

Add the parsley and a grinding of black pepper. Toss briefly. Pour into two large warmed bowls, making sure each gets plenty of the broth. Serve immediately with thick chips and crusty bread for mopping.
